subject: Mathematics
board: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9–1) Mathematics (1MA1), Higher tier
source: School Maths folder: Edexcel GCSE (9–1) Mathematics content, sequenced using the school's two-year scheme order (decimals and recurring decimals, powers and roots, surds, algebraic manipulation, formulae, linear equations and inequalities); Edexcel 1MA1 Higher exam style; INSET lesson standard.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Number: decimals, powers and roots
lessons.title: Recurring decimals and fractions
lessons.bigQuestion: Can every fraction be written as a decimal, and every decimal as a fraction?
objectives: Know which fractions give terminating or recurring decimals
Convert a fraction to a recurring decimal
Convert a recurring decimal to a fraction using algebra
successCriteria: Write fractions as recurring decimals using dot notation
Convert simple recurring decimals such as 0.4̇ to fractions
Convert decimals like 0.12̇7̇ to fractions and show the method in 1MA1 style
lessons.crossCurricular: Computing: why computers store some fractions inexactly
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: infinity in a finite-looking number; wonder at mathematical structure

keywords.def: a decimal that ends, such as 0.375
a decimal with a digit or block of digits repeating forever
dots over the first and last repeating digits
a number that can be written as a fraction of two integers

starter: Write 0.35 as a fraction in its simplest form

teach.heading: Terminating or recurring?
bullets: Denominator with only prime factors 2 and 5: terminates
teach.note: Examples: 7/40 (40 = 2³ × 5) terminates; 5/12 (12 = 2² × 3) recurs. Ask pupils to predict before calculating.

teach.heading: Recurring decimal to fraction
bullets: Multiply by 10ⁿ to line up the repeats
Subtract to cancel the recurring part
teach.note: This is the method the mark scheme expects: show both lines and the subtraction.

teach.heading: A non-repeating start
bullets: Multiply to move the non-repeating part first

teach.heading: Wrong multiplier
teach.note: Show the error and how the decimals fail to cancel.

misconception.right: Use 100x so the blocks line up: 99x = 27

check.q: Which fraction gives a terminating decimal?
check.why: 20 = 2² × 5, so 9/20 = 0.45. 6, 15 and 21 each have a factor of 3 (or 7), so they recur.

practice: Write 0.4̇5̇ as a fraction in its simplest form
independent: Core: Convert to fractions in their simplest form: (a) 0.8̇ (b) 0.3̇6̇ (c) 0.1̇2̇3̇
Extend: Show that 0.16̇ = 1/6 and that 0.24̇ = 11/45
Stretch: Prove that 0.9̇ = 1 using algebra, and explain why this is not a rounding error.
lessons.homework: Exam practice: four 1MA1-style 'show that' recurring-decimal questions (3 marks each) from the homework sheet.
lessons.send: Support: method frame with the two lines to complete. Stretch: proofs about rational and irrational numbers.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Number: decimals, powers and roots
lessons.title: Prime factors, HCF and LCM
lessons.bigQuestion: How can prime factors solve real problems with timings and sharing?
objectives: Write numbers as products of prime factors in index form
Find HCF and LCM using prime factors
Solve HCF and LCM problems, including given in index form
successCriteria: Write a number as a product of prime factors
Find HCF and LCM using a Venn diagram
Find HCF and LCM of numbers given in index form without working them out
lessons.smsc: Social: planning fair shares and schedules

keywords.def: a number written as a product of primes
using powers, e.g. 2³ × 5
highest common factor
lowest common multiple

teach.heading: Product of primes
bullets: Write in index form, in order

teach.heading: HCF and LCM in index form
bullets: HCF: lowest power of each common prime
LCM: highest power of every prime

model.problem: A = 2³ × 3² × 5 and B = 2² × 3⁴ × 7. Find the HCF and LCM.

teach.heading: Mixing up highest and lowest
bullets: HCF divides into both, so use the lower powers
teach.note: Ask pupils to check: does 36 divide into A = 360 and B = 2268? Yes: 360 = 36 × 10 and 2268 = 36 × 63.

check.why: Highest power of each prime: 2⁴, 3³ and 5. A is the HCF; C adds the powers; D misses the 5.

practice: Find the HCF and LCM of 84 and 90
independent: Core: Find the HCF and LCM of (a) 120 and 150 (b) 2² × 3 × 5² and 2 × 3³ × 5
Extend: Two runners lap a track in 72 s and 84 s. They start together. After how many minutes are they next together at the start line?
Stretch: x = 2ᵃ × 3 and y = 2³ × 3ᵇ. HCF(x, y) = 12 and LCM(x, y) = 216. Find a and b.
exit: Write 252 as a product of primes.
lessons.homework: 1MA1 past-paper style: five HCF/LCM questions, including two in index form.
lessons.send: Support: Venn template. Stretch: number of factors of a number from its prime factors.

keywords.def: 1 divided by the number
a^(1/n) means the nth root of a
the inverse of a power
find the value

starter: What is any non-zero number to the power 0?

teach.heading: Why a half power is a square root
bullets: So 9^(1/2) is the number that squares to 9
teach.note: Answer the big question using the multiplication law. Then 8^(1/3) = ∛8 = 2.

teach.heading: The three-step method
teach.note: Root first keeps the numbers small.

teach.heading: Negative index error
bullets: A negative index never makes the answer negative

teach.heading: Writing as a power
teach.note: Exam questions ask: write 1/√8 as a power of 2: 8 = 2³, √8 = 2^(3/2), so 2^(−3/2).

check.why: Fourth root of 16 is 2, and 2³ = 8. A multiplies 16 by 3/4; D treats the index as negative.

practice: Write 1/x⁴ as a power of x
independent: Extend: Find n: (a) 2ⁿ = √32 (b) 9ⁿ = 1/27 (c) 4ⁿ × 8 = 2¹¹
Stretch: Write √(2⁷) × 4^(−1/4) as a power of 2.
exit: Write ∛x² as a power of x

cannot be written as a fraction of integers
an answer left as a surd, not a rounded decimal
a factor that is a square number

check.why: 48 = 16 × 3, so √48 = 4√3. A is not fully simplified; C does not root the 16.

independent: Extend: A rectangle has sides √18 cm and √8 cm. Find its area and perimeter in exact form.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Number: decimals, powers and roots
lessons.title: Expanding brackets with surds and rationalising

objectives: Expand brackets containing surds
Rationalise denominators of the form a/√b
Rationalise denominators of the form a/(b + √c)

keywords.def: remove the surd from the denominator
the same expression with the sign between terms changed, e.g. 3 + √5 → 3 − √5
not rounded
(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²

teach.heading: Rationalising a/√b
teach.note: 6/√3 = 6√3/3 = 2√3. Answer the big question: exact values are easier to compare and add when the denominator is rational.

teach.heading: Using the conjugate
bullets: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate
The bottom becomes a difference of two squares

teach.heading: Only multiplying the bottom
bullets: Top and bottom must be multiplied together
teach.note: Show how multiplying only the denominator changes the number.

check.why: 10√5/5 = 2√5. A forgets the surd on top; C forgets to divide by 5.

independent: Core: (a) Expand (5 − √2)(5 + √2) (b) Rationalise 12/√6 (c) Rationalise 3/√7
Extend: Rationalise 6/(√5 − 1) and simplify.
Stretch: Show that (√3 + 1)/(√3 − 1) can be written as a + √b where a and b are integers. Find a and b.
lessons.homework: Edexcel GCSE 1MA1 Higher-style surds exam questions (Paper 1H/2H) from the sheet, with full working.

Expand the product of three binomials
Simplify the results

keywords.def: an expression with two terms
an expression with highest power 3
multiply out brackets
terms with the same letters and powers

teach.heading: Three binomials: two stages
bullets: Multiply the result by the third
teach.note: Answer the big question: a cubic can describe a volume, e.g. a box with sides (x + 1), (x + 2), (x − 3).

check.why: Expansion is x³ + 5x² + 2x − 8. The x² coefficient is 2 − 1 + 4 = 5.

independent: Core: Expand and simplify (a) (4x − 1)(2x + 3) (b) (x + 4)(x − 2)(x − 1)
Extend: Show that (x + 3)(2x − 1)(x − 2) = 2x³ + x² − 13x + 6
Stretch: A box has dimensions (x + 2), (x + 3) and (2x − 1) cm. Expand to find its volume and evaluate it when x = 4. Check by multiplying the dimensions directly.

the number multiplying a term
the number without a letter

Two numbers multiply to −10 and add to 3?

bullets: Find p and q: product c, sum b

teach.heading: Using signs
bullets: c positive: same signs (sign of b)

steps: c is negative: one positive, one negative

Use the splitting-the-middle-term method
Check by expanding
successCriteria: Factorise fully when there is also a common factor

keywords.def: rewrite bx as two terms so you can factorise in pairs
the product of the x² coefficient and the constant
take common factors from pairs of terms
an expression with highest power 2

starter: Two numbers multiply to 6 and add to 7?

teach.heading: Splitting the middle term
bullets: Find two numbers: product ac, sum b
Split bx into those two terms

teach.heading: Why it works
bullets: We are rebuilding those four terms
teach.note: Show the grid: 6x², −4x, 3x, −2. The middle split is exactly the two middle cells.

teach.heading: Brackets that don't match
bullets: Signs in the second pair must make the same bracket

check.why: (3x + 4)(x + 2) = 3x² + 6x + 4x + 8 = 3x² + 10x + 8. A gives 14x; C gives 11x; D gives 25x.

independent: Core: Factorise (a) 2x² + 9x + 4 (b) 5x² − 13x − 6 (c) 6x² + 11x + 3

keywords.def: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
no bracket can be factorised further
a number or term that is a square, e.g. 9x²
a factor shared by every term

teach.heading: Choosing a method
bullets: Always take out a common factor first
teach.note: Display the decision flow and refer to it all lesson.
cycle: Check: can any bracket factorise again?

teach.heading: Factorising fully
bullets: Keep going until nothing more factorises

steps: x² − 4 is also a difference of squares

teach.heading: Sum of two squares
bullets: x² + 9 does not factorise over real numbers

check.why: 5(x² − 9) then difference of squares. A is not fully factorised; B is correct but not fully factorised; D is wrong.

independent: Core: Factorise fully (a) x² − 100 (b) 4x² − 9 (c) 18 − 2x² (d) x² − 6x − 27

divide top and bottom by the same factor
something that multiplies the whole expression
no common factors remain

Terms are added: never cancel them

misconception.right: x is a term, not a factor; (x + 6)/x does not simplify

independent: Core: Simplify (a) (3x + 12)/(x + 4) (b) (x² − 9)/(x² − 3x) (c) (x² − x − 6)/(x² − 9)

change the subject of a formula
